healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Croatia. Emergency numbers (112/194/192/193), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance, and vaccination recommendations for travelers.

medications.prescriptionRules: EU prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside the EU may need verification from a local doctor. Croatia has adopted EU pharmaceutical standards. Some medications more freely available than in some other EU countries.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substance. Requires prescription or doctor approval. Small quantities for personal use may be brought with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled opioid. Requires prescription or doctor consultation in Croatia. Carry your foreign prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. EU regulations apply. Carry doctor's letter and original prescription. Customs may inspect quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Methylphenidate (Ritalin) and ADHD medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Requires documentation. Contact Croatian health authorities or your embassy if you need to bring ADHD medications.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal for recreational use and strictly controlled medically. CBD products with zero THC are legal. Do not bring any THC-containing products.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Croatian or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU citizens should carry EHIC. Non-EU travelers should carry prescriptions and a multilingual medical certificate.

connectivity.simOptions: A1, T-Mobile, or Telemach at airports. EU roaming works since 2023.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Good WiFi at cafes, hotels, restaurants along coast.
connectivity.bestOption: EU SIM with roaming. Otherwise A1 prepaid at airport.

cultural.tipping: 10% at restaurants appreciated. Round up for taxis.
cultural.dressCode: Casual on coast. Cover shoulders/knees in churches. Comfortable shoes in Old Towns.
cultural.greetings: Handshake formal. Kiss on both cheeks between friends. 'Bok' is casual hello.
taboos: Being loud in Old Towns at night
Not trying local wine when offered

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen, joined 2023). UK, EU, Australia, Canada also visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: May-June and September (warm, fewer crowds). July-August peak in Dubrovnik.

stalenessWarnings.message: Some data in this profile may be outdated. Connect to the internet to refresh.

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 192)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (192) and ambulance (194) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
